introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper. Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D.
incertitudes: Q1 passée en ouverte : « calcul », « calculatrice » et « calculateur » sont chacun défendables après « sans » pour un ingénieur ; aucune lettre désignée (calculatrice est la plus probable).

Q34 passée en ouverte : A « Prevention is better than cure » (proverbe équivalent) et B « It is better to prevent than to treat » (traduction littérale) sont toutes deux justes ; aucune lettre désignée (A est la plus probable pour le Board).

Clés retenues mais à relire : Q11 d chargeaient (seule forme accordée avec « les hommes »), Q22 d donc (or introduit un argument et non une conséquence), Q18 d sommes allés (masculin pluriel par défaut), Q25 b à cause des (en raison de est imprimé sans « des »), Q50 b bread winner.

Recopié tel qu’imprimé : consignes en anglais pour Q46 à Q50 ; Q4 option A « un » apparaît soulignée sur le scan (marque de candidat, ignorée) ; Q13, Q35 et Q38 balisent l’expression soulignée par <u>...</u> ; Q43 « 5h15 » est en italique dans le sujet ; Q29, Q34 et Q41 sont des questions de traduction glissées parmi les questions de grammaire.

Q44 : l’option D « huit » est imprimée en haut de la page 4, séparée des options A à C en bas de la page 3 ; elle appartient bien à la Q44. Q37 : le complément « les cheveux » est placé après le verbe, donc participe invariable.

Scan photocopié avec filigrane (gcerevision.com) ignoré : accents et élisions relus sur le rendu en image, aucune zone illisible. Les blancs imprimés en traits sont écrits « ____ ». La virgule manquante dans le passage (« Fatima, une fille brave avait toujours rêvé ») est recopiée telle qu’imprimée.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Il est difficile pour un ingénieur de travailler sans ____.

*Options as printed:* A) calcul B) calculatrice C) calculateur D) calculateurs
questions.corrige_markdown: Three options fit the sentence: "sans calcul" (without calculation), "sans calculatrice" (without a calculator, the most natural everyday object) and "sans calculateur" (without a calculating device or computer, a technical term used in engineering). Only "calculateurs" (plural, with no article) is unlikely. Because several options are defensible, no letter is designated. Rule: after "sans", a singular noun is used without article.

questions.enonce_markdown: Mon oncle est riche ____ il n’achète pas des livres à ses enfants.
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence contrasts his wealth with his not buying books, so the conjunction of opposition "mais" is needed. "Car" gives a cause, "ou" an alternative and "ni" needs a preceding negation. Rule: mais = but, it introduces a contrast. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Le sport ____ les peuples.
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence needs a conjugated verb in the present indicative, third person singular, with the subject "le sport": "unit" (unir). "Unis" would go with je or tu, "uni" and "unie" are participles. Rule: the verb agrees with its subject (3rd person singular, -it). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Avec ____ moto, on peut facilement faire des courses.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Moto" is a feminine noun, so the feminine indefinite article "une" is required: "avec une moto" (with a motorbike). "Un" is masculine, "de" and "de la" are not used before a countable noun here. Rule: the article agrees in gender with the noun. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Ma voisine a acheté de ____ habits pour ses filles.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Habits" is masculine plural. With the plural indefinite article, "des" becomes "de" before an adjective, and the adjective is masculine plural: "de beaux habits". "Belle" and "belles" are feminine and "beau" is singular. Rule: the adjective agrees with its noun in gender and number. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Tu as achevé ton exercice ____ temps.
questions.corrige_markdown: The fixed expression "à temps" means in time, on time. "A" without an accent is the verb avoir, "en temps" and "dans temps" do not exist. Rule: à temps = in time (fixed preposition). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Pour ____ le Covid-19, il faut observer les mesures barrières.
questions.corrige_markdown: After the preposition "pour", the verb is in the infinitive: "pour éviter". The other forms are imperative, participle or present indicative and cannot follow "pour". Rule: preposition + infinitive. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Il me faut ____ pain pour la salade.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Il me faut" is followed by a quantity of something uncountable: the partitive article "du" (masculine "pain"): "il me faut du pain". "Dû" is a participle, "le" would mean a specific loaf and "de" is used only after a negation or an expression of quantity. Rule: the partitive du/de la names an unspecified quantity. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Pour remonter le moral des malades, le médecin leur parle ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: To raise the patients' morale, the doctor speaks to them kindly: "gentiment". "Méchamment" (nastily), "gravement" (gravely, seriously) and "intensément" (intensely) do not express encouragement. Rule: choose the adverb whose meaning fits the purpose of the action. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Le mécanicien ____ on parlait hier vient d’arriver.
questions.corrige_markdown: The verb "parler de" needs the preposition "de", so the relative pronoun is "dont" (of whom): "le mécanicien dont on parlait". "Donc" is a conjunction, "que" is a direct object and "qui" is a subject. Rule: dont replaces de + antecedent. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Les hommes ____ les bagages dans le bus avant le départ.
questions.corrige_markdown: The only form that agrees with the third person plural subject "les hommes" is "chargeaient" (imperfect, an action in progress before the departure). "Chargez" is for vous, "charges" for tu and "charger" is an infinitive. Rule: the verb agrees with its plural subject (-aient). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
- As-tu vu ma fille ?
- Oui, je ____ ai vue.
questions.corrige_markdown: The direct object pronoun "la" (replacing "ta fille") is elided before the vowel of "ai": "je l'ai vue". The past participle "vue" agrees with the feminine object placed before the verb. "Lui" is an indirect object, "la" without elision and "le" are wrong. Rule: la/le become l' before a vowel. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Pendant les examens, il a <u>passé des nuits blanches</u>. L’expression soulignée veut dire :
questions.corrige_markdown: "Passer une nuit blanche" is an idiom meaning to spend the night without sleeping. "À la belle étoile" means sleeping outdoors, which is a different idiom. Rule: an idiom is understood as a whole, not word by word. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Passer des nuits à la belle étoile.

questions.enonce_markdown: J’ai acheté des bijoux ____ or pour mon anniversaire.
questions.corrige_markdown: To indicate the material something is made of, French uses "en": "des bijoux en or" (gold jewellery). "D'or" is literary and does not fit this plain sentence, "à or" and "de l'or" are wrong. Rule: en + material. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Après la proclamation des résultats, nous organiserons une fête ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: The party is organised after the results are announced, so a time marker relative to that event is needed: "le lendemain" (the next day). "Demain" is tied to the moment of speaking, "la veille" means the day before and "l'aube" is dawn. Rule: le lendemain = the day after a given date. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: En courant, l’enfant s’est fracturé ____ jambe.
questions.corrige_markdown: With a reflexive verb followed by a part of the body, French uses the definite article, not the possessive: "s'est fracturé la jambe". "Sa" is not used because the reflexive pronoun already shows possession. Rule: reflexive verb + body part takes the definite article. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Tu ____ à la sueur de ton front.
questions.corrige_markdown: The subject is "tu", and the sentence is a future statement ("you will eat by the sweat of your brow"): "mangeras". "Mangera" is third person, "mangerais" is the conditional (or imperfect) and "mangerait" is third person. Rule: tu + future ends in -as. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Jean et moi ____ prendre les cours dans les clés USB.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Jean et moi" is equivalent to "nous", so the auxiliary is "sommes". The group includes Jean (masculine), so the participle takes the masculine plural: "allés". Rule: with être, the participle agrees with the subject; a group including a man = masculine plural. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Elle a eu une blessure et le ____ coule abondamment.
questions.corrige_markdown: A wound makes the blood flow: "le sang". "Cent" (hundred), "sans" (without) and "sent" (from sentir) are homophones that do not fit. Rule: homophones are told apart by meaning and grammatical function. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Les marchandises que j’ai ____ sont déjà au port.
questions.corrige_markdown: The direct object "que" stands for "les marchandises" (feminine plural) and precedes the verb, so the past participle agrees: "commandées". Rule: with avoir, the participle agrees with a direct object placed before the verb. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: J’aimerais vivre jusqu’à ____ ans.
questions.corrige_markdown: The number 80 is written with a hyphen, "quatre-vingts", and takes an -s because nothing follows it in the number (the noun "ans" comes after the whole number). Rule: quatre-vingts takes -s when nothing follows it in the number. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - numbers and fractions

questions.enonce_markdown: Le réseau téléphonique est mauvais ____ les téléchargements sont lents.
questions.corrige_markdown: The slow downloads are the consequence of the bad network, so the conjunction of consequence "donc" is needed. "Ni" needs a negation, "mais" introduces a contrast and "or" introduces an argument, not a result. Rule: donc = therefore. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Mon grand frère a ____ amis dans l’enseignement.
questions.corrige_markdown: After an adverb of quantity such as "beaucoup", the preposition "de" is used, and it is elided before a vowel ("amis"): "beaucoup d'amis". "Beaucoup des" is wrong and "beaucoup" alone lacks the preposition. Rule: adverb of quantity + de (d' before a vowel). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: « Le coup de fil a été reçu par Sam ». À la voix active cette phrase devient :
questions.corrige_markdown: The passive verb "a été reçu" is in the passé composé, so the active verb must keep the same tense with the agent "Sam" as subject: "Sam a reçu le coup de fil". The other options change the tense. Rule: passive to active keeps the tense; the agent becomes the subject. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

choix.texte: Sam a reçu le coup de fil.
Sam reçoit le coup de fil.
Sam recevra le coup de fil.
Sam recevait le coup de fil

questions.enonce_markdown: J’ai raté mon vol ____ embouteillages en ville.
questions.corrige_markdown: The missed flight is a negative result caused by the traffic jams: "à cause des" (because of). "Grâce aux" is for a positive cause, "à force des" is not idiomatic and "en raison de" is incomplete because the plural noun needs "des" (en raison des). Rule: à cause de = negative cause; grâce à = positive cause. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Je fais la lessive en ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: After "en", the gerund ("en chantant", while singing) expresses two simultaneous actions by the same subject. "Chante" and "chanta" are conjugated forms and "chant" is a noun. Rule: en + present participle = gerund. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Si tout le monde dormait sous une moustiquaire, on ne ____ plus du paludisme.
questions.corrige_markdown: The "si" clause is in the imperfect ("dormait"), so the main clause takes the conditional present: "on ne parlerait plus". Rule: si + imperfect, then conditional (hypothesis). **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Je souhaite que tu ____ vite.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Souhaiter que" is followed by the subjunctive. The present subjunctive of "guérir" with "tu" is "guérisses". "Guéris" is the indicative or imperative and "guérisse" is for je, il or elle. Rule: souhaiter que + subjunctive. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: « You have the floor » peut être traduit en français par :
questions.corrige_markdown: In a debate, "to have the floor" means to be allowed to speak: "avoir la parole". The other options translate the words literally (floor = plancher, sol) or give a different meaning (it is your turn, option D). Rule: translate an idiom by its equivalent, not word by word. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - translation into French

questions.enonce_markdown: Simon est architecte. Demande-____ d’apprécier ton plan.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Demander à quelqu'un de faire": the person asked is an indirect object, so the pronoun is "lui" (to him). "Le" is a direct object, "la" is feminine and "leur" is plural. Rule: demander à + person = indirect pronoun (lui). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Ce terrain a une superficie de cinq ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: A superficie (area) of land is measured in hectares. "Hectogrammes" and "kilogrammes" are units of mass and "mètres" is a unit of length. Rule: choose the unit that matches the quantity measured (area: hectare). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Mon amie est ____ dans une entreprise.
questions.corrige_markdown: The noun for a woman who works in computing is "informaticienne" (feminine of informaticien). "Informaticien" is masculine, "informatique" is the field or an adjective and "informateur" means informant. Rule: the profession noun agrees with the gender of the person. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: L’arbitre ____ quand Roger a marqué le but.
questions.corrige_markdown: The referee's whistling happened before another past action ("Roger a marqué"), so the pluperfect is needed: "avait déjà sifflé". "A déjà sifflé" is the passé composé (same time as the goal) and "avais" and "as" are first and second persons. Rule: pluperfect = action before another past action. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown:
« Mieux vaut prévenir que guérir » Could be translated into English as:

*Options as printed:* A) Prevention is better than cure. B) It is better to prevent than to treat. C) Let sleeping dogs lie. D) Once bitten twice shy.
questions.corrige_markdown: Two options are defensible: A is the standard English proverb with the same meaning, and B is a faithful literal translation of the sentence. C and D are other proverbs with different meanings (do not disturb a quiet situation; a bad experience makes you cautious). Because both A and B are correct translations, no letter is designated; the Board most probably expects A. Rule: a proverb is translated by its equivalent proverb or by its meaning.
themes: O Level French - translation into French

questions.enonce_markdown: Ma tante a <u>une langue de vipère</u>. L’expression soulignée signifie :
questions.corrige_markdown: "Avoir une langue de vipère" is an idiom meaning to speak maliciously, to say hurtful things about others. The other options take the words literally or are unrelated. Rule: an idiom is understood as a whole. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Avoir la langue d’un serpent venimeux.
Aimer la viande de la vipère.

questions.enonce_markdown: Dans ____ pays aura lieu la prochaine Coupe d’Afrique des Nations ?
questions.corrige_markdown: The interrogative adjective agrees with the masculine singular noun "pays": "quel pays". "Quelles", "quels" and "quelle" have the wrong gender or number. Rule: quel agrees in gender and number with its noun. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Elles ____ les cheveux avant d’aller à la fête.
questions.corrige_markdown: The verb is reflexive ("se peigner"), so the auxiliary is "être" with "se". The reflexive pronoun is an indirect object because the direct object "les cheveux" follows the verb, so the participle does not agree: "se sont peigné". Rule: with a reflexive verb, the participle agrees with a direct object only when it comes before the verb. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Ce match s’est achevé sur <u>un score de parité</u>. L’expression soulignée signifie :
questions.corrige_markdown: A "score de parité" is a tie, with both teams having the same number of goals: "deux-deux". The other scores show a winner. Rule: parité = equality. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: N’____ pas peur ma fille, l’injection ne fait pas mal.
questions.corrige_markdown: The speaker addresses one person ("ma fille") with the informal imperative: the imperative of "avoir" for "tu" is "aie" (irregular, without final -s), so "n'aie pas peur". "Ayez" (vous) and "ayons" (nous) do not fit, and "aies" is the subjunctive or indicative form. Rule: imperative of avoir, 2nd person singular = aie. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: ____ eau n’est pas potable.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Eau" is feminine, so the demonstrative adjective is "cette", even though the noun starts with a vowel. "Cet" and "ce" are masculine and "c'est" is a pronoun with the verb être. Rule: cette precedes a feminine noun. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: “The policeman caught the thief red-handed” Could be translated into French as:
questions.corrige_markdown: "To catch someone red-handed" is translated by the idiom "prendre quelqu'un la main dans le sac". The other options translate the words literally and give absurd meanings (a bag in the hand, a red hand). Rule: translate an idiom by its French equivalent. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - translation into French

choix.texte: Le policier a pris un bandit avec un sac à la main.
Le policier a arrêté la main rouge d’un bandit.
Le policier a arrêté un bandit avec la main rouge.
Le policier a pris le bandit la main dans le sac.

questions.enonce_markdown: J’ai ramassé une clé USB en classe. Est-ce ____ ?
questions.corrige_markdown: The possessive pronoun replaces "clé" (feminine singular) and the question is addressed to "tu": "la tienne". "Le tien" is masculine singular and "les tiens" and "les tiennes" are plural. Rule: the possessive pronoun agrees with the noun it replaces. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Le docteur a insisté que je sois à l’hôpital à 5h15. 5h15 en toutes lettres donnera :
questions.corrige_markdown: 15 minutes past the hour is "et quart", so 5h15 is "cinq heures et quart". "Et demie" is 5h30 and "moins" gives times before the hour (5h moins quinze is 4h45). Rule: heure + et quart = 15 minutes past. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - numbers and fractions

questions.enonce_markdown: Pendant la course, il est arrivé après les huit premiers coureurs, alors il est le ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: Arriving after the first eight runners means finishing ninth, and a rank is expressed with an ordinal number: "neuvième". "Huitième" is eighth, and "neuf" and "huit" are cardinal numbers that cannot give a rank after "le". Rule: ordinal numbers (-ième) express rank. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - numbers and fractions

questions.enonce_markdown: Voici la salle informatique ____ nous faisons cours.
questions.corrige_markdown: We hold lessons "in" the computer room, so the relative pronoun is "dans laquelle" (feminine singular, agreeing with "salle"). "De laquelle", "pour laquelle" and "à laquelle" do not express the place where lessons are given. Rule: preposition + lequel/laquelle agrees with the antecedent. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Passage for questions 46 to 50**

Fatima, une fille brave avait toujours rêvé de suivre ses frères à l’école. Elle était victime du sort réservé aux filles ; l’analphabétisme. Seuls les garçons avaient le privilège d’accéder à l’éducation. Face à cette injustice sociale, Fatima ne cessait de questionner son père, qui un jour, avait cédé à son vœu le plus cher. A l’école, Fatima s’est avancée à grands pas. Aujourd’hui, grâce à son emploi et un salaire d’ingénieur, sa famille entière mange à sa faim.

Which of the following virtues does not reflect Fatima’s character?
questions.corrige_markdown: Fatima is described as "brave" (courageous), she kept asking her father until he agreed (determined) and she supports her family (good). Nothing in the passage says she prays or is religious. Rule: a comprehension answer must be supported by the text. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

Why was Fatima not attending school at first?
questions.corrige_markdown: The text says that she was a victim of the fate reserved for girls and that only boys had the privilege of access to education, so the society did not favour girls' education. Nothing mentions hatred of school, her age or lack of money. Rule: the answer must come from the text. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Her society was not in favour of the girl child education.
Her parents could not afford the resources.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

How did she finally get to school?
questions.corrige_markdown: The text says that she never stopped questioning her father, who one day gave in to her dearest wish; she therefore persuaded him. Rule: the answer must come from the text. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: The society revised its hard rules.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

Describe her performance in school.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Fatima s'est avancée à grands pas" is figurative and means that she progressed quickly, so she made great strides in her studies. Option B takes the expression literally, which is the trap. Rule: figurative expressions are not taken literally. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: She made great strides in her studies.
She walked fast daily to reach her school.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

How helpful is she to her family?
questions.corrige_markdown: Thanks to her job and an engineer's salary, her whole family has enough to eat, so she supports the family financially: she is the breadwinner. Being an engineer is her job and does not describe how she helps, and the text does not say she cooks or advises. Rule: the answer must come from the text. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: She is an engineer in her family.
She prepares food for her family.
